subpages.text: Platform Solutions Resources Company Get a demo Contact sales Platform Solutions Resources Company Contact sales Get a demo All posts The market is already sending signals. The advantage is connecting them first Product · July 30, 2026 · 6 min read MT Marketing Team Product The market for public tenders produces a constant stream of signals. Every day a contracting authority publishes a tender notice, a contract is awarded, a competitor gains ground in a category where it had no presence before, and demand rises in one region while it slows in another. This is public information, and in theory anyone could read it. For a company or distributor that takes part in tenders, the problem is therefore not access to the data, but how to piece it together. The signals arrive scattered, at different times and from different sources, and taken on their own they say little. The full picture, the one that really matters when deciding which markets to focus on and with what strategy, almost always stays out of reach. The picture is there, but scattered Rebuilding that picture today takes hours of manual work. The information lives on different platforms and in different formats, award data sits in separate documents, and competitor moves can only be reconstructed by cross-referencing several sources. On top of this sits a subtler but more serious limit: the method is never comprehensive. Working by hand, you cover only the portion of the market you can keep up with, and whatever lies beyond it stays invisible, often without you even realising it. The result is that the information exists, but the full picture does not. Slow insight has a cost This work is costly not only for the time it takes, but for the delay it imposes on decisions.
